title: trial-engagement-sprint-outline-and-resource-log
content:
Purpose and scope:
This is the working sprint-outline and resource log for the upcoming customer trial engagement (external: Acme Financial Services). The goal is to validate Redwood inference performance and operational fit for a low-latency chat summarization feature integrated into Acme's claims portal. This doc tracks workstreams, per-sprint milestones, owners, resource commitments, risks, and workshop notes.

Engagement objectives (success criteria):
- End-to-end demo: integrated chat summarization in Acme staging by EOW Sprint 3.
- Latency SLO: 95th percentile token generation latency <= 250ms for 512-token windows under representative load.
- Cost guidance: provide estimated per-session cost at 10k DAU traffic profile.
- Security: private deployment network proof of concept with customer KMS integration.
- Quality: no semantic regression vs baseline (measured on 200 prompt eval set; target >= 0.88 human-agreement score).

High-level timeline (6-week engagement):
- Sprint 0 (Prep, 4 days): kickoff, env access, data intake, initial latency profiling plan.
- Sprint 1 (Week 1, 5 working days): model selection + baseline runs, basic integration stub, workshop #1 (requirements deep-dive).
- Sprint 2 (Week 2, 5 working days): performance tuning (batching/caching), quantization trial, gateway routing setup, workshop #2 (ops runbook).
- Sprint 3 (Week 3, 5 working days): end-to-end staging integration, security review, run acceptance evals.
- Sprint 4 (Week 4, 5 working days): stress tests at scale, cost estimation, deliver final handoff deck and runbook.
- Buffer (Week 5-6): contingency for blockers, additional tuning, formal handoff and exec demo scheduling.

Task tracker (working list, owners, current status):
- K0: Kickoff & NDAs: Owner: Priya Nair; Status: done; Notes: NDA signed 2025-01-06.
- K1: Env access checklist (staging creds, VPC peering request): Owner: Ravi Kapoor; Status: in_progress; Due: Sprint 0 end; Blockers: firewall rules pending (ticket INF-119).
- T1: Data contract & sample prompts (200 eval prompts): Owner: Noah Chen; Status: in_review; Notes: customer delivered sample set 2025-01-10, need normalization script.
- T2: Baseline model runs (latency + throughput): Owner: Ava Martinez; Status: todo; Acceptance: produce 95p latency table and request-level traces.
- T3: Integration shim (REST -> Redwood API connector): Owner: Sofia Alvarez; Status: todo; Notes: include token accounting headers.
- T4: Smart batching & cache config experiment: Owner: Ravi Kapoor; Status: todo; Metrics: cost/token, 95p latency at 1, 5, 10 concurrent sessions.
- T5: Quantization trial + perf delta doc: Owner: Noah Chen; Status: todo; Linked PR: GITHUB:repo/redwood-trial-configs/pull/14.
- T6: Private KMS integration test: Owner: Priya Nair; Status: todo; Risk: requires customer security review window.
- T7: Workshop materials + agenda (2 workshops): Owner: Ava Martinez; Status: in_progress; Deliverable: slide deck + hands-on lab instructions.
- T8: Cost model for 10k DAU (sheet): Owner: Sofia Alvarez; Status: todo; Link: CONFLUENCE:ENG/SE/trial-playbook.

Resource commitments (estimated):
- Solutions engineering: 0.5 FTE week1-3, on-call for week4 demo prep.
- Applied-ML: 0.25 FTE for quantization and perf analysis in sprint2.
- Platform SRE: 8 hours over sprints 0-2 for VPC peering and firewall.
- Customer E2E test support: 1 product engineer from Acme for sprints 2-3.

Workshop notes (initial drop-in, 2025-01-09):
- Attendees: Acme product lead (Karen Li), Acme infra (Tom R.), Redwood SE (Ava, Ravi, Sofia), Security (Priya).
- Goals: align on low-level integration points, acceptance criteria, and data sensitivity constraints.
- Outcomes / action items:
  - Acme to provide data schema and sample payloads by 2025-01-10 (assigned Tom R.).
  - Redwood to produce a 30-minute hands-on lab for workshop #2 showing batching configs (Ava, due Sprint 2 day 2).
  - Security to schedule KMS architecture call (Priya + Acme security) by 2025-01-12.

Risk register (live, concise):
- R1: Network access delays (probability: medium) -> Impact: blocks integration testing. Mitigation: request firewall rules early; maintain a public-stubbed integration for early E2E tests.
- R2: Customer data sensitivity prevents sample export (probability: low-medium) -> Impact: reduces ability to run evals locally. Mitigation: propose on-prem data adapter or synthetic prompt generation.
- R3: Quantization causes quality regression (probability: low) -> Impact: fails acceptance. Mitigation: keep quantization optional path and measure on eval set; rollback plan.
- R4: SRE capacity squeeze during stress test window (probability: medium) -> Impact: delayed stress runs. Mitigation: coordinate early and limit runs to off-peak windows.

Acceptance checklist for final deliverable:
- Integration validated in Acme staging with end-to-end flow (demo runbook executed).
- Performance report (latency percentiles, throughput curves) delivered and reviewed.
- Cost sheet + recommendations handed off.
- Security checklist completed and KMS test passing.
- Workshop artifacts (slides, lab scripts) uploaded to Confluence.

Communication plan:
- Weekly status summaries in Slack #se-trials-thread (owner: Ava).
- Twice-weekly syncs (Mon/Wed 30m) during sprints 1-3.
- Major blockers escalate to Platform Eng manager via email and JIRA ticket.

Open questions & decisions to make (tracked):
- Q1: Which model family do we pick for baseline? (options: Llama-2-Chat-like quantized vs opt-family) -> Decision owner: Ava; target decision Sprint 1 day 2.
- Q2: Will Acme accept per-request metadata headers for tracing? (affects instrumentation) -> Action: confirm in Sprint 0.

Appendix: quick links and artifacts
- Confluence playbook: CONFLUENCE:ENG/SE/trial-playbook
- Jira backlog epic: JIRA:SE-4821
- GitHub config PR: GITHUB:repo/redwood-trial-configs/pull/14
- Slack channel: #se-trials-thread

Notes to self (working):
- Keep this doc minimal for customer sharing; maintain a separate internal runbook with full run traces and perf dumps.
- Revisit cost assumptions if Acme plans >100k sessions/day.

Last updated: 2025-02-11 by Ava Martinez
